$comment: How a theme document is *stored* — SPEC §20. Onyx has two backends: the
engine (src-tauri/src/settings.rs, normalise_theme_doc) and the mock the
browser preview and the screenshot harness run against (src/lib/mock.ts).
Both are held to this file:
Storage is the only opinion either backend has about a theme; what a
`text` is the argument to set_theme_doc. `build` makes the long inputs a
literal cannot carry: `unit` repeated `times`, with `prefix` in front.
`stored` is what must come back out of the snapshot; `"=input"` means the
input unchanged. `rejected: true` means the command must fail loudly.

cases.name: comments and newlines survive — a theme is source, not data
an empty box clears the theme
a C1 control is refused — Cc does not stop at U+007F
a vertical tab is refused — only tab, LF and CR lay a document out
a non-breaking space is text, not whitespace, and is kept
a leading BOM is kept — JS trims it, Rust does not, so neither may
a lone NEL is a control character, not blankness
one byte over the limit is refused
the limit counts bytes, not characters
100k characters that fit in the byte budget are stored
